gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at today's maker-store prices, one 20-lb propane tank in EcoFlow's $689 Smart Generator 3000 (Dual Fuel) holds about 20 kWh by EcoFlow's own figure. A battery-only 1 kWh station costs $459–$549 (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic $459, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 $499, Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 $549) and holds about one-twentieth of that per charge.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results or catalog cards, so there were no cited rival pages to compare against. Its own answer gives only overlapping cost ranges ('$300–$2,000+' vs '$400–$2,000+') and one runtime example (1,000 Wh runs 100 W for 8–9 h). It names no models, gives no prices and does not compare energy per dollar or per tank of fuel, so nothing it showed the shopper covers this.
decides: For multi-day home outages it settles the choice on a fuel generator, or a generator paired with a station: at about $0.42–$0.56 per stored Wh (today's maker prices below), matching one 20 kWh propane tank with batteries would cost several thousand dollars. For camping, indoor use or short outages it confirms the station, because the generator is not sold in California (CARB) and EcoFlow rates it at 69 dB at 23 ft against about 25–30 dB for the stations. EcoFlow's generator can auto-start and stop only with DELTA 3, DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Ultra Plus, so the best value is the hybrid rather than an either-or choice.
